conviction_note: The findings add up to +1.0: H1 looks strong (Q1 OP at 28.7% of the 10.0bn plan, Q2 average USD/JPY about 159 against a 150 plan assumption, management told analysts Q2 would stay firm). That is mostly offset by three things: Maxell has held its OP guide at every H1 print for three years (once with 61% progress), IFIS consensus already sits about 15% above the plan, and the stock fell after 9 of its last 11 real prints. So p_up is only 53 on a 4.5% scale, which scales to +0.27. The gap to the +1.0 sum is the guidance coin flip: a raise and a hold have opposite signs and roughly equal odds.
bar: IFIS consensus FY3/27 ordinary profit 11,491m JPY (kabuyoho/IFIS, data updated 2026-10-28, https://kabuyoho.jp/reportNews?bcode=6810&cat=3). After Q1 ordinary profit of 3,127m, it implies about 2.8bn a quarter for Q2-Q4. The company plan is OP 10,000m / NP 6,700m with no H1 split (Q1 tanshin https://f.irbank.net/pdf/20260731/140120260724599100.pdf). print_vs_bar is my estimate of Q2 ordinary profit against that roughly 2.8bn implied run-rate; no published Q2 consensus was found.
positioning_check: JPX disclosed short register: 0.0% (no position at or above 0.5%), unchanged, as of 2026-10-28 (baseline, https://www.jpx.co.jp/markets/public/short-selling/index.html). Margin ratio 2.57x, leveraged retail moderately long (kabutan https://kabutan.jp/stock/?code=6810, 2026-10-29). No option market, so no skew. IFIS rating consensus 3.00 (neutral) and target-price consensus 2,420 JPY, below the 2,515 spot. Goldman Sachs crossed 5% on 2026-09-07 and fell back below 5% on 2026-09-25; GMO (Grantham Mayo) raised its holding in June. No short fuel, and a mild long overhang.

findings.finding: H1 is set up for an above-plan print that puts pressure on the 10.0bn FY OP guide: Q1 OP was 2,872m (28.7% of plan, against 25% at the same point last year), Q2 average USD/JPY was about 159 (77bank fixings Jul 162.56 / Aug 158.94 / Sep 156.39) against the 150 assumption, and the Maxell Sakura (ex-Murata primary-battery business) consolidation has raised FX sensitivity. But in three years Maxell has never raised OP at an H1 print; it held at 61% H1 progress in FY3/24 and held in FY3/25 and FY3/26. A raise toward the street's roughly 11bn is plausible but well short of certain.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: H1 prints that held OP: 2023-10-30 +0.31%, 2025-10-31 -1.12%. 2024-10-31 cut sales: -9.27%. FY guide below consensus on 2026-04-27: -8.37%. Q1 beat by about 1bn against consensus on 2026-07-31: +24.15% (Yahoo daily closes, https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/6810.T?range=3y&interval=1d).
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: consensus 経常 rose from 10,198m (Aug) to 11,491m (Oct), so the street already marks above the plan, and the stock has held about 2,500 since the Q1 jump. What is not priced is whether the company itself raises. A held guide is Maxell's documented habit (kabuyoho revision history), so the street cannot price a raise as base case. If a raise were priced, the stock would have run up into the print; instead the 20-day move is -2.6% and the 5-day move +0.2%.
findings.independence: FX: 77bank daily fixings https://www.77bank.co.jp/kawase/usd2026.html. 150-yen assumption and higher FX sensitivity: Fisco via kabutan https://kabutan.jp/stock/news?code=6810&b=n202608030488 (2026-08-03). Revision habit: https://kabuyoho.jp/report?bcode=6810. Three different sources, but they all bear on one decision.

findings.finding: Management told analysts on 2026-07-31 that the analog-core businesses would stay 'broadly firm' in Q2: adhesive-tape inventory stocking driven by the Middle East would continue through Q2 and calm in H2, semiconductor DMS would stay strong on AI/datacentre demand, and silver costs had eased with pass-through restoring energy margins from H2. That points to a Q2 near or above the street-implied run-rate of about 2.8bn ordinary profit.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: A quarter-level surprise of about 1bn against consensus moved the stock +24.15% on 2026-08-03 (limit-up). In-line quarters have drawn -1% to -5%.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the briefing is public and consensus moved up after it. What is left is the size of the tape stocking in Q2, which management called a special factor. The street may model it fading earlier than management said. If it were fully priced, consensus TP (2,420) would not sit below spot.
findings.independence: Q1 tanshin segment text (same company, separate document) describes the same tape stocking and semiconductor recovery: https://f.irbank.net/pdf/20260731/140120260724599100.pdf

findings.finding: There is no shareholder-return catalyst scheduled for this print. Under MEX26 (FY3/25-FY3/27) the ≥100% total payout has already been reached (13.2bn buyback in FY3/26), the 2026-04-27 progress report says further buybacks will be considered 'flexibly' in light of results, and the interim dividend is planned at 28 JPY. Cash fell and short-term borrowings rose in Q1. Last year's buyback came on 2025-11-17 via ToSTNeT-3, not with the H1 release. A buyback announced at this print is a low-probability upside tail.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The 2025-11-17 ToSTNeT-3 buyback was announced separately from the print; no H1-print buyback in the last three years (irbank IR list).
findings.why_not_priced: Nobody is positioned for a buyback at this print because the payout target is already met and the balance sheet is funding doubled capex. If one were expected, it would be in the street commentary, and none was found.
findings.independence: IR filing list showing the 2025-11-17 timing: https://irbank.net/6810/ir

findings.finding: Positioning and reaction history lean against a rally on a merely good print: the stock fell after 9 of its last 11 real release dates, and the one big rally (+24% on Q1) came from a 1bn beat against a 1.7bn consensus. Target-price consensus 2,420 sits below spot, the rating consensus is neutral at 3.00, the margin ratio of 2.57 is long-tilted, and there are no disclosed shorts to squeeze.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: it is public positioning, and the margin overhang is already in the baseline lean (-0.205). Kept small because the selling-the-print pattern is a reaction function, not a fact about this quarter.
findings.independence: Yahoo daily closes for the reaction history: https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/6810.T?range=3y&interval=1d; release dates from Maxell IR calendar https://www.maxell.co.jp/ir/event/ir_calendar.html

outside_window.finding: Last year's buyback came by ToSTNeT-3 on 2025-11-17, about two and a half weeks after the H1 print. A similar post-print buyback under the 'flexible' policy would land after the exit window.

baseline_tension: The evidence leans slightly positive against a near-flat priced lean (-0.08) and a -2.6% 20-day run-up, so it does not merely agree with positioning. The strongest positive the release could carry is an OP raise toward 11bn plus a buyback; I looked for both and neither is signalled. The strongest negative is a hold on a Q2 helped by one-off tape stocking, in a name that has sold most of its prints.
lessons_applied: Rule 1 (a negative resting on a series the market already has, p_up toward 50): the positioning/reaction-history negative rests on public consensus TP and the margin ratio, which the baseline lean already carries, so it was trimmed from -0.6 to -0.4. p_up was already 53 and was left there.
Rule 2 (negatives outnumbering positives): did not bind, with three positives and one small negative. The strongest positive (a raise plus buyback) was looked for and is recorded in baseline_tension.
Nothing else changed: the guidance, quarter and capital-return findings and abs_move_pct stand as drafted.
